algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

Below is a practical “road‑map” you can follow – from choosing your technology stack all the way through to deploying a production‑ready storefront. Feel free to skip sections that already fit what you’re doing; I’ve kept it modular so you can cherry‑pick as needed. --- ## 1️⃣ Define Your Requirements & Constraints | Question | Why It Matters | |----------|----------------| | **Target devices** (desktop only, mobile first, PWA?) | Determines layout strategy & tooling. | | **Performance budget** (e.g., < 2 s load time) | Influences bundle size, lazy loading, CDN usage. | | **SEO needs** (product pages indexed by Google?) | Decides between client‑side rendering vs SSR / SSG. | | **Accessibility goals** (WCAG AA/AAA?) | Guides component library choice & testing approach. | | **Team skill set** (JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Vue…) | Avoid steep learning curves. | | **Budget/timeframe** | Helps decide if you’ll use a headless CMS + static site generator or roll everything yourself. | > *Tip:* Write down a short spec sheet before picking frameworks—this keeps decisions aligned with business priorities rather than just technical hype. --- ## 2️⃣ Pick a Frontend Stack ### Core Framework | Option | Strengths | When to Use | |--------|-----------|-------------| | **Next.js (React)** | Built‑in SSR/SSG, file‑based routing, image optimisation, easy API routes. | SEO heavy sites, fast startup, rich ecosystem. | | **Nuxt.js (Vue)** | Similar benefits to Next but for Vue. | If team prefers Vue over React. | | **SvelteKit** | Smaller runtime, faster compile times, great developer ergonomics. | Want minimal JS payload, modern feel. | | **Remix** | Focuses on progressive enhancement, fine‑grained control over caching. | Complex data flows, server‑first UX. | *If you prefer pure SPA without SSR*: plain Create‑React‑App, Vite+React, or Vue CLI will do, but keep SEO in mind. ### Styling System | Choice | Notes | |--------|-------| | **Tailwind CSS** | Utility‑first, highly composable, works well with any framework. | | **Material‑UI / MUI** | Ready‑made components, theming support. Good for rapid prototyping. | | **Chakra UI** | Accessible out‑of‑the‑box, simple styling props. | | **Styled Components / Emotion** | Scoped styles via tagged template literals. Great when you want full CSS-in-JS flexibility. | ### State Management | Tool | Typical Use Case | |------|------------------| | **Redux Toolkit** | Large global store, complex cross‑component interactions. | | **Zustand / Jotai** | Tiny stores, less boilerplate. | | **Recoil** | Fine‑grained atom selectors, good for async derived states. | | **React Query / TanStack Query** | Server state (API calls), cache invalidation, optimistic updates. | For most e‑commerce UIs, combining `react-query` (or its equivalent in other ecosystems) with a lightweight local store (`zustand`) gives you both robust remote data handling and quick UI reactivity. --- ## 3️⃣ Design Architecture ``` src/ ├─ app/ # Pages/routes (SSR/SPA) │ └─ product/[slug].tsx ├─ components/ # Reusable UI pieces │ ├─ ProductCard.tsx │ ├─ Navbar.tsx │ └─ CartIcon.tsx ├─ hooks/ # Custom hooks (useCart, useAuth, ...) ├─ lib/ # Utilities (api clients, auth helpers) ├─ context/ # Context providers (ThemeProvider, AuthContext) ├─ services/ # Business logic (cart service, checkout flow) └─ assets/ # Images, icons, fonts ``` ### Key Patterns | Pattern | What it solves | |---------|---------------| | **Feature‑folder structure** | Keeps related files together → easier onboarding. | | **Container–Presentational split** | Separates concerns: container fetches data, presentational renders UI. | | **Atomic Design** | Consistent component hierarchy (atoms → molecules → organisms). | | **Server‑Side Rendering (SSR)/Static Generation (SSG)** | Improves initial page speed & SEO. | | **Code Splitting/Lazy Loading** | Only loads chunks required for current route. | --- ## 4️⃣ Build Core Features | Feature | Implementation Tips | |---------|---------------------| | **Product Listing Page** | • Paginate or infinite scroll.
• Filter/sort controls (price range, categories).
• Use `` component from Next/Image for automatic resizing. | | **Product Detail Page** | • Show high‑res images with zoom overlay.
• Add-to-cart button triggers cart hook.
• Display reviews/comments fetched asynchronously. | | **Shopping Cart** | • Persist cart in localStorage + sync with backend session.
• Optimistic UI update on add/remove.
• Show subtotal, tax estimate live. | | **Checkout Flow** | • Multi‑step wizard (shipping address → shipping method → payment → review).
• Integrate Stripe Elements or Braintree Drop‑In UI.
• Validate form fields with Yup/Zod. | | **User Authentication** | • OAuth (Google/Facebook) + email/password.
• Store JWT in HttpOnly cookie for security.
• Protect protected routes with higher‑order component or middleware. | | **Search Bar** | • Debounce input (300ms).
• Call Algolia or ElasticSearch endpoint.
• Highlight matched terms. | | **Responsive Navigation** | • Mobile hamburger menu with slide‑out panel.
• Sticky header on desktop. | | **Dark Mode** | • Theme provider toggles class on root element.
• Persist preference in localStorage. | | **Analytics** | • Inject GA4 tag or Plausible analytics script.
• Track events: view_product, add_to_cart, purchase. | --- ## 5️⃣ Connect to Backend APIs Assuming you have a RESTful or GraphQL API: ```ts // src/lib/apiClient.ts import axios from 'axios'; const api = axios.create({ baseURL: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL || '/api', }); export const getProducts = () => api.get('/products'); export const getProductBySlug = (slug: string) => api.get(`/products/${slug}`); export const addToCart = (itemId: number, qty: number) => api.post('/cart', { item_id: itemId, quantity: qty }); ``` Use `react-query`: ```ts import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'; import { getProducts } from '@/lib/apiClient'; function ProductsList() { const { data, error, status } = useQuery(['products'], getProducts); if (status === 'loading') return ; if (error) return ; return (
{data.map(product => ( ))}
); } ``` This pattern automatically handles caching, refetching, and background updates. --- ## 6️⃣ Accessibility Checklist | Checkpoint | How to Verify | |------------|--------------| | Semantic HTML tags (`header`, `nav`, `main`, `footer`). | Inspect DOM tree. | | ARIA labels where necessary (buttons, modals). | Use axe-core extension. | | Keyboard navigation focus order. | Tab through entire page manually. | | Contrast ratios ≥ 4.5:1 (text) / 7:1 (large text). | Color contrast checker. | | Alt attributes on images. | Review markup. | | Skip‑to‑content link at top. | Test screen reader. | Run automated tests nightly with `jest-axe`. --- ## 7️⃣ Performance Optimization | Technique | Description | |-----------|-------------| | **Tree shaking** | Ensure bundler removes unused exports. | | **Dynamic imports** | Lazy‑load non‑critical modules (`next/dynamic`). | | **Critical CSS extraction** | Inline above‑fold styles. | | **Image optimisation** | Serve WebP, AVIF, auto‑resize. | | **Service Worker** | Cache assets, enable offline mode. | | **Bundle analyzer** | Visualise module sizes (`webpack-bundle-analyzer`). | | **Prefetch links** | Hint browser to prefetch next page resources. | Measure baseline with Lighthouse, then iterate until hitting target scores (>90 overall). --- ## 8️⃣ Testing Strategy | Layer | Tests | |-------|-------| | Unit | Jest + React Testing Library for individual components/hooks. | | Integration | Mock API responses, test interaction flows (add to cart, checkout). | | E2E | Cypress or Playwright scripts covering critical paths (login → buy). | | Snapshot | Capture visual regressions with Storybook + Chromatic. | | CI/CD | Run tests on GitHub Actions or CircleCI after each PR. | Example unit test: ```js test('renders product card title', () => { render(); expect(screen.getByText(/Test Shirt/i)).toBeVisible(); }); ``` --- ## 9️⃣ Deployment Pipeline | Step | Tool | Reason | |------|------|--------| | Code repo | GitHub/GitLab | Version control & collaboration. | | Linting/Formatting | ESLint + Prettier | Enforce style consistency. | | Continuous Integration | GitHub Actions | Automated lint/test/build runs. | | Static Site Hosting | Vercel (for Next.js) or Netlify | Zero‑config deployments, instant rollback. | | Edge Caching | Cloudflare Workers | Reduce latency globally. | | Monitoring | LogRocket or Sentry | Real‑time crash reporting. | | Analytics | Plausible or Matomo | Privacy‑friendly metrics. | Sample GitHub Action workflow snippet: ```yaml name: Deploy on: push: branches: [ main ] jobs: deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v2 - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile - run: pnpm run build - uses: vercel-action@master with: vercel-token: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }} vercel-org-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }} vercel-project-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID }} alias-domains: example.com,www.example.com ``` --- ## 🔧 Quick Starter Template (Next.js + Tailwind) Create project: ```bash npx create-next-app@latest ecommerce-demo --typescript cd ecommerce-demo npm i tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer npx tailwindcss init -p ``` Configure `tailwind.config.cjs`: ```js module.exports = { content: ['./pages/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}', './components/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}'], theme: { extend: {} }, plugins: [], }; ``` Add basic navbar component: ```tsx // components/Navbar.tsx export default function Navbar() { return (
Shop
  • Store
  • About
) } ``` Now start dev server: ```bash npm run dev ``` Your skeleton is ready! From here plug in the patterns described earlier. --- ## 📌 Final Takeaway Checklist 1. **Define scope** → device targets, SEO, accessibility, timeline. 2. **Choose stack** → framework, styling system, state manager. 3. **Set up folder structure** → feature‑centric, reusable components. 4. **Implement core features** → listings, detail, cart, checkout, auth. 5. **Hook into backend** → typed API client + react‑query. 6. **Ensure accessibility** → semantic markup, ARIA, keyboard nav. 7. **Optimize performance** → lazy load, image optimisations, SWR. 8. **Write tests** → unit, integration, end‑to‑end. 9. **Automate CI/CD** → lint, test, build, deploy. 10. **Monitor & Iterate** → real‑world feedback loop. Happy coding—and may your storefront convert visitors into customers! 🚀

We can provide steps: choose tech stack (React/Vue/Angular), design UI/UX, responsive design, component architecture, state management, API integration, authentication, payment gateway integration, performance optimization, testing, deployment.

We might also ask clarifying questions about their preferences or constraints. But we could give general advice.
